arxiv-2204-09266.title: Hessian Averaging in Stochastic Newton Methods Achieves Superlinear Convergence
arxiv-2204-09266.creator: Sen Na, Michał Dereziński, Michael W. Mahoney
arxiv-2204-09266.description: Abstract We consider minimizing a smooth and strongly convex objective function using a stochastic Newton method. At each iteration, the algorithm is given an oracle access to a stochastic estimate of the Hessian matrix. The oracle model includes popular algorithms such as Subsampled Newton and Newton Sketch, which can efficiently construct stochastic Hessian estimates for many tasks, e.g.

arxiv-2211-16783.title: Modelling of Spintronic Terahertz Emitters as a function of spin generation and diffusion geometry
arxiv-2211-16783.creator: Yingshu Yang, Stefano Dal Forno, Marco Battiato
arxiv-2211-16783.description: Abstract Spintronic THz emitters (STE) are efficient THz sources constructed using thin heavy-metal (HM) and ferromagnetic-metal (FM) layers. To improve the performance of the STE, different structuring methods (trilayers, stacked bilayers) have been experimentally applied. A theoretical description of the overall THz emission process is necessary to optimize the efficiency of STE.

arxiv-2304-07368.title: Möbius carbon nanobelts interacting with heavy metal nanoclusters
arxiv-2304-07368.creator: C. Aguiar 1, N. Dattani 2,3, I. Camps 1,3
arxiv-2304-07368.description: Abstract To investigate the interaction between carbon and Mobius-type carbon nanobelts and nickel, cadmium, and lead nanoclusters, we utilized the semiempirical tight binding framework provided by xTB software. Through our calculations, we determined the lowest energy geometries, complexes stability, binding energy, and electronic properties.

arxiv-2409-17055.title: DRIM: Learning Disentangled Representations from Incomplete Multimodal Healthcare Data
arxiv-2409-17055.creator: Lucas Robinet, Ahmad Berjaoui, Ziad Kheil, Elizabeth Cohen-Jonathan Moyal
arxiv-2409-17055.description: Abstract Real-life medical data is often multimodal and incomplete, fueling the growing need for advanced deep learning models capable of integrating them efficiently. The use of diverse modalities, including histopathology slides, MRI, and genetic data, offers unprecedented opportunities to improve prognosis prediction and to unveil new treatment pathways.

arxiv-2411-15793.title: Sharp estimates for Jacobi heat kernels in double conic domains
arxiv-2411-15793.creator: Dawid Hanrahan
arxiv-2411-15793.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dawid Hanrahan. We study the even and odd Jacobi heat kernels defined in the context of the multidimensional double cone 𝕍 d + 1 \mathbb{V}^{d+1} and its surface 𝕍 0 d + 1 \mathbb{V}^{d+1}_{0} , the multidimensional hyperboloid 𝕍 d + 1 ϱ \prescript{}{\varrho}{\mathbb{V}^{d+1}} and its surface 𝕍 0 d + 1 ϱ \prescript{}{\varrho}{\mathbb{V}^{d+1}_{0}} , and the multidimensional paraboloid 𝕍 ~ d + 1 \widetilde{\mathbb{V}}^{d+1} and its surface 𝕍 ~ 0 d + 1 \widetilde{\mathbb{V}}^{d+1}_{0} .

arxiv-2506-03593.title: Is linguistically-motivated data augmentation worth it?
arxiv-2506-03593.creator: Ray Groshan*, Michael Ginn*, Alexis Palmer
arxiv-2506-03593.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ray Groshan*, Michael Ginn*, Alexis Palmer. Data augmentation, a widely-employed technique for addressing data scarcity, involves generating synthetic data examples which are then used to augment available training data. Researchers have seen surprising success from simple methods, such as random perturbations from natural examples, where models seem to benefit even from data with nonsense words, or data that doesn’t conform to the rules of the language.

arxiv-2506-05061.title: A Survey on Vietnamese Document Analysis and Recognition: Challenges and Future Directions
arxiv-2506-05061.creator: Anh Le, Thanh Lam, Dung Nguyen
arxiv-2506-05061.description: Abstract Vietnamese document analysis and recognition (DAR) is a crucial field with applications in digitization, information retrieval, and automation. Despite advancements in OCR and NLP, Vietnamese text recognition faces unique challenges due to its complex diacritics, tonal variations, and lack of large-scale annotated datasets.

arxiv-2506-16380.title: Classification of Cattle Behaviour and Detection of Heat(Estrus) using Sensor Data Thanks: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
arxiv-2506-16380.creator: Druva Dhakshinamoorthy † \dagger, Avikshit Jha † \dagger, Sabyasachi Majumdar, Devdulal Ghosh, Ranjita Chakraborty, Dr. Hena Ray
arxiv-2506-16380.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel approach to cattle behavior detection and detection of Estrus(heat) periods using sensor data and machine learning techniques. By employing an affordable Bluetooth-based monitoring system, we aim to enhance livestock management and improve animal welfare.

pmc-10548721.title: First field and laboratory evaluation of LAMP assay for malaria diagnosis in Cubal, Angola
pmc-10548721.creator: Begoña Febrer-Sendra, Beatriz Crego-Vicente, Arlette Nindia, Joan Martínez-Campreciós, Sandra Aixut, Alejandro Mediavilla, Aroa Silgado, Inés Oliveira-Souto, Fernando Salvador, Israel Molina, Antonio Muro, Elena Sulleiro, Pedro Fernández-Soto
pmc-10548721.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundMalaria is a globally distributed infectious disease. According to the World Health Organization, Angola is one of the six countries that account for over half the global malaria burden in terms of both malaria cases and deaths. Diagnosis of malaria still depends on microscopic examination of thin and thick blood smears and rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), which often lack analytical and clinical sensitivity. Molecular methods could overcome these disadvantages.

pmc-10722011.title: Transformers in medical image segmentation: a narrative review
pmc-10722011.creator: Rabeea Fatma Khan, Byoung-Dai Lee, Mu Sook Lee
pmc-10722011.description: Background and ObjectiveTransformers, which have been widely recognized as state-of-the-art tools in natural language processing (NLP), have also come to be recognized for their value in computer vision tasks. With this increasing popularity, they have also been extensively researched in the more complex medical imaging domain.

pmc-11654324.title: The impact of a short-term high-fat diet on coagulation function in a mouse model and its role in exacerbating concanavalin A-induced liver injury
pmc-11654324.creator: Eri Nanizawa, Yuki Tamaki, Tomiko Yakura, Shun Otsuka, Naoyuki Hatayama, Munekazu Naito
pmc-11654324.description: BackgroundRecently, the number of patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its more advanced condition, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), has been increasing. These patients are at a higher risk of cardiovascular events and thromboembolism. However, the direct impact of high-fat diet (HFD), a cause of MASLD, on liver coagulation function is not well understood.

pmc-11692410.title: Challenges in Diagnosis and Treatment of Mandibular Florid Osseous Dysplasia: A Case Report
pmc-11692410.creator: Mohammed Essioti, Hind Boukaaba, Anouar Titou, Dounia Kamal
pmc-11692410.description: Florid osseous dysplasia (FOD) is a rare, benign fibro-osseous lesion primarily involving the mandible and maxilla, with a higher prevalence in middle-aged women of African or Asian descent. This article presents a case of mandibular FOD complicated by secondary infection, emphasizing clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and treatment strategies.

pmc-12430477.title: Intuitive Eating Intervention in Physically Active Adults: Effects on Anthropometry, Athletic Performance, Eating Attitudes, and Body Image
pmc-12430477.creator: Meltem Pırıl Şenol, Ece Öneş, Murat Baş, Gözde Arıtıcı Çolak, Pilar Aranda Ramírez
pmc-12430477.description: Background/Objectives: There is growing interest in non-diet approaches to support health, well-being, and performance in different populations. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of a 12-week intuitive eating (IE) intervention on participants’ body composition, body image, eating behaviors, and athletic performance. Methods: The study included both an intervention group and a control group.

pmc-12437083.title: Metacognitive Functioning and its Relationship with Clinical Insight and Functional Outcomes in Schizophrenia: The Role of Illness Duration
pmc-12437083.creator: C Brasso, A Carluccio, G Colli, C Montemagni, R Sgro, P Rocca
pmc-12437083.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionUnderstanding the complex interplay between cognitive and functional domains in schizophrenia is crucial for improving patient functional outcomes. Metacognition has emerged as a critical factor in the functioning and rehabilitation of individuals with schizophrenia.

pmc-12656475.title: Integrated Metabolomics and Transcriptomics Analyses Reveal the Critical Role of Caffeic Acid in Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) Cold Tolerance
pmc-12656475.creator: Xiang Li, Guonan Fang, Yongzhen Ma, Wang Su, Shenglong Yang, Yun Zhou, Yanping Zhang, Jian Wang
pmc-12656475.description: Owing to the high altitude and short frost-free period of the Tibetan Plateau, potato plants are frequently exposed to cold stress (CS), which severely restricts their growth and productivity. Thus, understanding the mechanisms underlying cold tolerance in potato varieties is crucial for breeding improvement.

pmc-12734692.title: Deazaalloxazines – Flavin Derivatives That Provide Reductive Photoredox Catalysis with Inert Substrates
pmc-12734692.creator: Ivana Weisheitelová, Naisargi Varma, Ludmila Šimková, Josef Chudoba, Tetiana Pavlovska, Iwona Gulaczyk, Gotard Burdziński, Jiří Ludvík, Marek Sikorski, Radek Cibulka
pmc-12734692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Reductive transformations of substances that are difficult to reduce continue to pose challenges for photoredox catalysis. Promising photoreduction catalysts include flavin and deazaflavin derivatives; however, even their reductive abilities are limited for the range of substrates considered “inert”. In this work, we present 5‐deazaalloxazines, a new group of deazaflavin analogues that are predisposed to catalyze reductions due to their low reduction potential (down to −1.65 V vs. SCE) even in the ground state.

pmc-13148065.title: Structural and functional properties of gluten proteins in air-classified sprouted wheat flour and their impact on steamed gluten quality
pmc-13148065.creator: Jun Pan, Shaoying Li, Fengcheng Wang, Jie Zheng, Zhiyi Liu, Ke Bian, Zhenxiang Guo, Jiangtao Lin, Jiping Wen, Xiaoxiao Qi, Jia Guo
pmc-13148065.description: Sprouting markedly alters the properties of wheat gluten proteins, thereby influencing their functional behavior during steaming. In this study, sprouted wheat flour was separated by air classification into three particle-size fractions: F1 (>45 μm), F2 (20–45 μm), and F3 (<20 μm).

pmc-13482819.creator: Qin Shen, Chen Mei, Yidan Chen, Qian Zhang, Qingzhe Wu, Xinyuan Yu, Fei Zhang, Shengduo Liu, Chen Chen, Cunqi Ye, Qi Zhang, Xin-Hua Feng, Li Shen, Hai Song, Tingbo Liang, Penghong Song, Bing Xia, Pinglong Xu
pmc-13482819.description: EGFR hotspot mutations (mEGFR), including primary L858R, exon 19 deletion, and secondary T790M, are pivotal oncogenic drivers in human non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). At the same time, NSCLC resistance to third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is a major clinical challenge and remains mechanistically unresolved.

pmc-13554271.title: Quantitative assessment of thoracolumbosacral orthosis efficacy on the temporal features of gait using inertial measurement unit sensors
pmc-13554271.creator: Zahra Gull, Asim Waris, Xing Chen, Muhammad Anees Ijaz, Muhammad Jawad Khan, Muhammad Adeel Ijaz, Falah Alanazi, Khalid Ansari, Syed Omer Gilani
pmc-13554271.description: Prolonged sitting with poor spinal posture alter the biomechanics of spine and the whole body, alleviating gait efficiency and causing fatigue. Evidence suggest that spinal braces can correct postural deviations, enhance proprioception, postural control, and spinal stability. However, the impact of an abnormal posture and spinal brace on the temporal features of gait remains unexplored.

pmc-13604477.title: Applications of Acoustic Waves in Micro-Droplet Technologies
pmc-13604477.creator: Jianing Liu, Lijun Chen, Zheng Peng, Zachary B. Cluff, Pam Van Ry, Joseph Rich, Ruoyu Zhong
pmc-13604477.description: Acoustofluidics has emerged as a powerful technique for the precise generation, sorting, manipulation, and stimulation of cell-laden droplets within emerging droplet microfluidic studies. Droplet acoustofluidics leverages various mechanisms, including acoustic radiation forces and acoustic streaming, to actively manipulate droplets non-invasively. The remarkable speed, precision, and biocompatibility of acoustic waves make it an ideal tool for droplet-based single-cell-level biomedical research.

uslaw-usc-t25-s2210.title: 25 U.S.C. § 2210 — Tax exemption
uslaw-usc-t25-s2210.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s2210.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 24 (Indian Land Consolidation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. All lands or interests in land acquired by the United States for an Indian or Indian tribe under authority of this chapter shall be exempt from Federal, State and local taxation.

uslaw-usc-t42-s1320.title: 42 U.S.C. § 1320 — Approval of certain projects
uslaw-usc-t42-s1320.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s1320.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 7 (Social Security); Subchapter XI (General Provisions, Peer Review, And Administrative Simplification); Part A (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. No payment shall be made under this chapter with respect to any experimental, pilot, demonstration, or other project all or any part of which is wholly financed with Federal funds.

uslaw-usc-t48-s1414.title: 48 U.S.C. § 1414 — Exclusive privileges of discoverer
uslaw-usc-t48-s1414.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t48-s1414.description: United States Code, Title 48 (Territories And Insular Possessions); Chapter 8 (Guano Islands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The discoverer, or his assigns, being citizens of the United States, may be allowed, at the pleasure of Congress, the exclusive right of occupying such island, rocks, or keys, for the purpose of obtaining guano, and of selling and delivering the same to citizens.
